sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: marker_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Marker objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Marker object.
    
    Example: marker_equality('python_version >= "3.6"', 'python_version >= "3.6"') -> True

tools.name: marker_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with Marker objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a Marker object.
    
    Example: marker_inequality('python_version >= "3.6"', 'python_version < "3.6"') -> True

tools.name: marker_intersection
tools.description: Combine two marker objects with logical AND. left: The left-hand side marker expression, right: The right-hand side marker expression. Example: marker_intersection('python_version >= "3.6"', 'os_name == "posix"') -> 'python_version >= "3.6" and os_name == "posix"'.

tools.name: marker_union
tools.description: Combine two marker objects with logical OR. left: The left-hand side marker expression, right: The right-hand side marker expression. Example: marker_union('python_version >= "3.6"', 'os_name == "posix"') -> 'python_version >= "3.6" or os_name == "posix"'.

tools.name: specifier_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Specifier objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Specifier object.
    
    Example: specifier_equality(">=1.0", ">=1.0") -> True

tools.name: specifier_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with Specifier objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a Specifier object.
    
    Example: specifier_inequality(">=1.0", "<2.0") -> True

tools.name: version_in_specifier
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a specifier. version: A version string to check against the specifier, e.g. '1.2.3' -> true for specifier '>=1.0'. specifier: A version specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0', '==1.2.3').

tools.name: specifier_set_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with SpecifierSet objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a SpecifierSet object.
    
    Example: specifier_set_equality('>=3.0', '>=3.0') -> True

tools.name: specifier_set_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with SpecifierSet objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a SpecifierSet object.
    
    Example: specifier_set_inequality(">=1.0", "<2.0") -> True

tools.name: version_in_specifier_set
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a specifier set. version: A version string to check against the specifier set, e.g. '3.2' specifier_set: A string representation of a specifier set (e.g., '>=3.0,!=3.1') -> true if version satisfies all specifiers in the set.

tools.name: specifier_set_intersection
tools.description: Find the intersection of two specifier sets. left: a string representation of the left specifier set, right: a string representation of the right specifier set. Example: specifier_set_intersection('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=1.5,<2.5') -> '>=1.5,<2.0'.

tools.name: tag_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Tag objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Tag object.
    
    Example:
    >>> tag1 = Tag('cp39', 'cp39m', 'linux_x86_64')
    >>> tag2 = Tag('cp39', 'cp39m', 'linux_x86_64')
    >>> tag_equality(tag1, tag2)
    True
tools.direct_call: packaging.tags.Tag(left['interpreter'], left['abi'], left['platform']) == packaging.tags.Tag(right['interpreter'], right['abi'], right['platform'])

tools.name: version_less_than
tools.description: Check if one version is less than another. version1: The first version string to compare, version2: The second version string to compare.

tools.name: version_less_equal
tools.description: Check if one version is less than or equal to another. left: The left-hand version string to compare, right: The right-hand version string to compare.

tools.name: version_greater_than
tools.description: Check if one version is greater than another. left_version: The left-hand version string to compare, right_version: The right-hand version string to compare.

tools.name: version_greater_equal
tools.description: Check if one version is greater than or equal to another. version1: The first version string to compare, version2: The second version string to compare.

tools.name: version_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Version objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example: version_equality("1.0", "1.0") -> True

tools.name: version_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with Version objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example: version_inequality("1.0", "1.1") -> True

tools.name: create_empty_version_range
tools.description: Create an empty version range. No version satisfies it. prereleases: Whether prereleases are allowed in the version range -> the empty version range

tools.name: create_full_version_range
tools.description: Create a full version range that accepts all PEP 440 versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to accept non-PEP 440 strings; prereleases: whether to include prerelease versions. Example: create_full_version_range() -> 'VersionRange(...)'.

tools.name: create_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Return the strict singleton range `{version}`. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '{1.0}'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: intersect_version_ranges
tools.description: Find the intersection of two version ranges. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier. Example: intersect_version_ranges('>=1.0', '<2.0') -> '>=1.0,<2.0'.

tools.name: union_version_ranges
tools.description: Find the union of two version ranges. version_range_a: First version range in PEP 440 format, version_range_b: Second version range in PEP 440 format. Example: union_version_ranges(">=1.0,<2.0", ">=2.0,<3.0") -> ">=1.0,<3.0".

tools.name: complement_version_range
tools.description: Get the complement of a version range. version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet, e.g. '>=1.0' -> '<1.0'.

tools.name: difference_version_ranges
tools.description:
Find the difference between two version ranges. version_range_a: First version range specifier string, version_range_b: Second version range specifier string.
    
    Example: difference_version_ranges(">=1.0", ">=2.0") -> ">=1.0,<2.0"

tools.name: check_version_range_subset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a subset of another. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier to check if range1 is a subset of it. >>> check_version_range_subset('>=1.5,<1.8', '>=1.0,<2.0') -> True

tools.name: check_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a superset of another. outer_range: A version range specifier string for the outer range (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0'). inner_range: A version range specifier string for the inner range (e.g., '>=1.5,<1.8'). Example: check_version_range_superset('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=1.5,<1.8') -> True.

tools.name: check_version_ranges_disjoint
tools.description: Check if two version ranges are disjoint. range1: First version range specifier, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: Second version range specifier, e.g. '>=2.0,<3.0'. -> True if ranges are disjoint, False otherwise.

tools.name: check_version_in_range
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained in a version range.
    
    :param version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
    :param version: The version string to check against the range
    :return: True if the version is contained in the range, False otherwise
    
    >>> check_version_in_range(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5")
    True

tools.name: check_version_in_base_specifier
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a base specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0.0'; version: The version to check against the specifier, e.g. '1.2.3'; prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions, e.g. True.

tools.name: check_version_in_specifier
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'. version: The version string to check against the specifier. prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. If None, follows PEP 440 defaults. >>> check_version_in_specifier('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: check_version_in_specifier_set
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a specifier set. specifier_set: A string representing the version specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The version string to check against the specifier set, prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.

tools.name: check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    Returns True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the specifier set is unsatisfiable, False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_subset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a subset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. >>> check_specifier_set_subset('>=3.12,<3.13', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_superset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a superset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. >>> check_specifier_set_superset('>=3.12', '>=3.12,<3.13') True

tools.name: check_specifier_sets_disjoint
tools.description: Check if two specifier sets are disjoint. specifier_set1: First specifier set string, specifier_set2: Second specifier set string. >>> check_specifier_sets_disjoint('<3.12', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: parse_version
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the :class:`Version` constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: canonicalize_package_name
tools.description: Canonicalize a package name. name: The name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonicalize_package_name('Django') 'django'

tools.name: canonicalize_version_string
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version as a string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=True becomes '1'.

tools.name: parse_wheel_filename
tools.description: Parse a wheel filename into its components. filename: The name of the wheel file, e.g. 'foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl' -> {'name': 'foo', 'version': '1.0', 'build': [], 'tags': ['py3-none-any']}.

tools.name: parse_sdist_filename
tools.description: Parse an sdist filename into its components. filename: The name of the sdist file, e.g. 'foo-1.0.tar.gz' -> {"name": "foo", "version": "1.0"}.
